questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: Front wheel wobbling or shaking the handlebars is usually caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
Improperly tightening the front wheel to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: Front wheel wobbling happens when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. Most wobbling is caused by improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It allows you more time to respond to hazards.
It prevents you from finding an escape route.
It provides space to maneuver your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. It also gives you room to safely move your motorcycle when needed.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Cars may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out of windows. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They make objects look farther away than they really are. Learn how your mirrors work if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Perform both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Perform one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to both swerve and brake to avoid a hazard, do them one at a time. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: A main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes is:

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is taking a turn too wide. This can cause the motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all other traffic and pedestrians go, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this can change based on traffic.

questions.question: What must a helmet have if the rider is under 21?

options.text: Reflective material.
Hearing protection.
Yellow color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective material.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, riders and passengers under 21 must wear an approved motorcycle helmet. The helmet must have a chin or neck strap. It must have reflective material on both sides. You need at least four square inches of reflective material, unless the helmet is made entirely of reflective material.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Go through the intersection slowly.
Let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely. Wait for a green signal before turning in your direction.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and moving slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of a small vehicle like a motorcycle. Drivers of larger vehicles may not accurately judge your real speed and location.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: Right side
Center
Left side

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is the safest position. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to dangers.
You have room to maneuver.
You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react quickly and move around hazards if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your turn signal once you complete your turn or lane change. A signal that stays on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: If parked cars are on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, you should ride:

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane. This avoids dangers like opening car doors and people stepping between parked cars. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane to give yourself the most space.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before turning?

options.text: To prevent a power change in the middle of the turn.
To keep both hands on the grips during the turn.
To keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a power change in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before starting a turn. Shifting during a turn can cause sudden power changes that skid the rear wheel. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Give you a way to escape.
Help you feel wind blasts.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you feel wind blasts.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should protect you from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It should stop other drivers from using your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What is the oily strip down the center of a lane?

options.text: You should only ride on it if another vehicle is in the lane with you.
It usually gives good traction for riding, except when it is raining.
You should always avoid it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually gives good traction for riding, except when it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is oily but usually gives enough traction for safe riding, except in rain. The strip is about two feet wide. Motorcyclists can ride on either side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, ride in which part of your lane?

options.text: Right
Center
Left

questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: Before passing another vehicle on the left, ride in the left part of your lane.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It links the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It is connected to the gears and brakes when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It links the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you use the rear brake pedal, it links the front and rear brakes together. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you see a hazard in the road, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid letting other drivers know you are there.
Change your speed as needed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid letting other drivers know you are there.
questions.explanation: To create more space and reduce danger, alert other drivers by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed for the situation and change your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go forward slowly.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to cross ahead of a train.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust it as you go.

questions.question: When should you keep a longer distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When the road surface is slippery.
When there is light traffic.
When you can see through the vehicles in front to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road surface is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need extra space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Keep at least a four-second distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply the front and rear brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, ride in which part of your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest place for a motorcyclist when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to not leave your lane.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may give poor traction.

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
The roadway under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet pavement, snow, ice, mud, gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.
